proposals.evidence_note: Own2015 retrospective,75–76, places the1971–72 ENS seminar beside prior reading of jointly authored Bourdieu/Passeron books; Passeron’s credit remains. Own2007 email answer published2008,162, confirms intellectual fidelity while requiring historical correction of concepts taken from other times and objects. This supports an acknowledged, specific resource rather than doctrinal obedience or formal dissertation supervision. Later critical disagreement remains separately represented. Original seminar and cited monographs unread.

proposals.relationship: Charle challenges the isolation of Manet in Bourdieu’s account of symbolic revolution, emphasizing collective artistic dissent, dealers and differentiated market dependence.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2025 article,paragraphs17–24, with qualifications28–31: Charle credits the project’s achievements and Bourdieu’s more nuanced warnings against romantic rupture accounts. The2013 posthumous volume combines lectures with an unfinished manuscript coauthored with Marie-Claire Bourdieu; Charle’s own participation in its collective editing does not erase that credit or the work’s unfinished state. Public ResearchGate reproduction of the author’s article was read; publisher OpenEdition routes presented an Anubis check and were not bypassed. Full2013 book and later impressionism conference contribution unread.
primary_locators: Charle2025, numbered paragraphs17–24, especially19,23–24, and28–31; reproduced generated PDF pages6–10; paragraph1 for coauthored manuscript and editorial role.

proposals.relationship: Charle and Roche jointly argue that Bourdieu’s historical sociology helps overcome academic divisions and requires historically situated concepts.
proposals.evidence_note: Their signed6February2002 Le Monde essay,printed16, jointly discusses Actes de la recherche, relations between sociology and history, historical treatment of concepts and comparative/transnational research. This is a specified shared argument, without inferred causal priority or identical positions elsewhere. Adjacent pieces by Honneth and Ernaux are separate authors’ work and are not assigned to Charle/Roche.
primary_locators: Le Monde,6February2002,printed16 (PDF page14 one-based), Pierre Bourdieu et l’histoire, byline and columns1–5, especially paragraphs beginning Le projet d’Actes and Nombre d’historiens.

proposals.relationship: Charle identifies methodological proximity to Noiriel’s sociohistory despite their different labels.
proposals.evidence_note: Own December2007 email answer,published2008,162, rejects an unproductive terminology dispute while appreciating Noiriel’s and Michel Offerlé’s work and the work in their collection. Offerlé and the collective publication programme retain credit; no shared organization, identical interpretation or personal influence is inferred from this limited comparison. The books and collection were not freshly read.
primary_locators: Pinault interview162, response to Considérez-vous que la querelle histoire sociale/sociohistoire.

proposals.relationship: As Bantigny explains, Charle adopts Hartog’s regimes of historicity to study the socially uneven advance of modernity across the long nineteenth century.
proposals.evidence_note: Explicit named scholarly mediation: Bantigny’s2013 review,opening paragraph ending with note3, identifies the conceptual resource and its historical application. Her account distinguishes adoption from debate about the concept. Hartog’s2003 book and2012 reedition are distinguished in her note3; Charle’s2011 monograph and Hartog’s underlying works remain unread here. Her mentions of Lévi-Strauss,Lefort and Koselleck describe Hartog’s antecedents, not proof of three direct transmissions to Charle.
primary_locators: Bantigny2013, opening discussion, paragraph beginning Christophe Charle fait sienne la réflexion, note3; pre-Concurrence des temps section.

proposals.relationship: Charle credits the merits of the Lieux de mémoire project but argues that its popularity returned historians to cultural and national frames.
proposals.evidence_note: Own December2007 answer,published2008,163–164, explicitly says that he participated without following the master-builder’s intended direction. The institutional bibliography identifies Pierre Nora as editor of the specific1986 and1992 Lieux volumes to which Charle contributed; the interview’s unnamed editor is identified through that metadata, not presented as an explicit spoken naming. This is a qualified objection to a project’s framing and reception, not a rejection of memory research or adjudication of every chapter. Original volumes unread.
primary_locators: Pinault interview163–164, answer beginning C’est une question un peu vaste, especially La montée en puissance through Italy/Germany; institutional bibliography entries Le Collège de France(1986) and Les grands corps(1992).
